summary: The admitted 12c v51 evaluation first differs at segment 0 step 117 only in the engulfing message: C says “It engulfs you!” while JS says “The fog cloud engulfs you!”. All 17,823 RNG entries match and the cursor differs only because the longer JS name advances the message position. Source trace: mhitu.c:gulpmu prints Monnam(mtmp) before swallow state changes; do_name.c:x_monnam selects “it” when canspotmon is false. js/mhitu.js:2325-2328 overrides the naming owner to consider only invisibility and mundetected state, so it names the fog cloud even when the hero is blind. Keep the occupied-square visibility workaround for sighted heroes, but preserve the canonical or explicitly injected visibility owner when blind.

source.branch: Bounded repair to the initial gulpmu engulfer message naming owner. Preserve explicit canSpotMonster/canSeeMonster owners; otherwise use canonical canspotmon for physical visibility and sensing in every state. Account for the occupied hero square only when the hero is sighted, the engulfer is at the hero coordinates, and mon_visible accepts the monster, matching C IN_SIGHT at that square. No whole gulpmu completion is claimed.
callers: mhitu.c:mattacku -> gulpmu(mtmp, mattk) for a monster engulfing the hero
mhitu.c:gulp_blnd_check -> gulpmu(u.ustuck, mattk) for swallowed engulf-blindness checks
dependencies: display.c:canspotmon combines canseemon and sensemon; both visibility and sensing must remain canonical when the hero is blind

evidence: Accepted evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-12c2941a9047cf5fc48e2f032217ecfbdb3884ba-v51.json reports 348/349 screens and cursors, 17,823/17,823 RNG calls; first mismatch is screen 117, row 0, column 39 (C “I”, JS “T”).

The admitted C screen at step 117 is “You multiply from its heat!  It dies!  It engulfs you!”; replaying the first 118 input steps in JS displays “You multiply from its heat!  It dies!  The fog cloud engulfs you!”. The unexpected article/name explains the cursor position mismatch; no source RNG or state divergence precedes it.

nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c:1334-1338 calls Monnam(mtmp) for the initial non-steed swallow line. nethack-c/upstream/src/do_name.c:863-865 sets do_it when !canspotmon(mtmp), yielding “it”; this branch runs before u.uswallow changes.

js/mhitu.js:2325-2328 injects canSpotMonster: () => !mtmp.minvis && !mtmp.mundetected, overriding the canonical visibility owner and incorrectly treating a blind hero as spotting the monster. js/do_name.js:973-982 trusts that injected owner. Keep the nonblind occupied-square workaround while giving blind heroes and explicit caller owners the C-equivalent visibility decision.

followupSourceReview.summary: The first correction fixed blindness but still used a sighted predicate that omitted See_invisible and sensing. The bounded naming owner now uses canspotmon(monster, state), plus the occupied-hero-square physical-visibility case only when the hero is not blind and mon_visible(monster, state) accepts the monster. This retains SEE_INVIS and hidden-monster rules while canspotmon retains detection, telepathy, and warning senses.
followupSourceReview.source: mhitu.c:1300-1338 removes and places the engulfer at u.ux/u.uy before Monnam; include/vision.h:28 defines cansee from IN_SIGHT; vision.c:663 and :672 mark the hero square IN_SIGHT for a sighted hero; display.h mon_visible applies See_invisible and mundetected; display.c canspotmon adds sensemon.
